label: copy-phase input e (fed-back e), from the 4th output onward
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the token e is the input during the copy phase, i.e. the model just output e and it is fed back (in_first=0; essentially zero activity on original-phase or delimiter steps, and on any other input token). Activation is gated by position in the copy: silent at recall_idx 0-1, weak/rare at recall_idx 2 (rate 0.5%), and fully on from recall_idx >= 3 (rate ~3.4% of all steps there, matching the share of e inputs). Adding recall_idx >= 3 lifts precision from 0.60 to 0.90 with 95% recall and 98% mass recall. Lower-quartile activations are early-copy e inputs (recall_idx 2-3, often e at original position 2); the strongest activations (~0.9-1.0 of max) are e inputs late in the copy (recall_idx ~5), often right after an x. Remaining false positives are mostly e at original position 2 fed back at recall_idx 3 in longer sequences. Does not depend on which token is output next, the first token, or digit count.

issues: The claim that the feature turns on at recall_idx 3 is a marginal artifact. Firing on copy-phase e depends on recall_idx and to_go (equivalently sequence length L) together, not on recall_idx alone. Precision of copy & e by cell: recall_idx 2 gives 1.00 at to_go 0 (412 steps), 0.94 at to_go 1 (2348), then 0.007 at to_go 2 and 0.0 at to_go 3-5. recall_idx 3 gives 1.00 at to_go 0-1, 0.85 at to_go 2, then 0.40 / 0.23 / 0.31 at to_go 3 / 4 / 5. recall_idx 4 gives 1.00 at every to_go.

Systematic miss class: an e fed back at recall_idx 2 in short sequences (L = 3-4, to_go <= 1) fires reliably, e.g. 'j e l <DEL> j [e:0.43]' and 't e y <DEL> t [e:0.25]'. The explanation calls this 'weak and rare', which only holds when averaged over all lengths.

Systematic false-positive class: an e fed back at recall_idx 3 in long sequences (to_go >= 3, i.e. L >= 7) is mostly inactive, at 23-40% precision. This is most of the predicate's roughly 6k test false positives. The explanation does note this, but the predicate does not handle it.

The rest checks out: activation is about 100% copy-phase mass; in_tok e holds 100% of mass (4 / 3 / 2 stray actives on a / 1 / m); the feature is silent at recall_idx 0-1 and on the delimiter step; it does not depend on out_tok or prev_tok (flat about 2x lift across tokens).

Refined predicate on test: precision 0.989, recall 0.951, F1 0.969, mass recall 0.994, vs the original's precision 0.894, F1 0.921. Remaining misses are weak (0.01-0.23) e inputs at recall_idx 3 in long sequences, which is scattered noise.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input e (fed-back e), from about the 3rd-4th output onward; switches on earlier in short sequences (on at recall_idx >= 4, or at recall_idx 2-3 when within 1-2 outputs of the end)
